title: Manchester United close to agreement with Kobbie Mainoo, Harry Maguire over new contracts
content:
Manchester United are close to an agreement with Kobbie Mainoo and Harry Maguire over new contracts.

Although work still needs to be done, negotiations are now at an advanced stage as United look to conclude fresh terms with both players.

Mainoo is currently tied down until June 2027 — with an option to prolong by 12 months — and the proposed extension would take him through to the summer of 2031 on a significantly improved salary.

The 20-year-old midfielder wanted to leave Old Trafford on loan after falling out of favour during Ruben Amorim’s tenure as head coach — although the club always insisted they wanted him to stay — but has returned to prominence under Michael Carrick and was called back into the senior England squad on Friday.

Maguire is scheduled to become a free agent at the end of this season, however a fresh one-year deal with an option to add an extra 12 months is in the process of being finalised.

Both players have started all nine of Carrick’s games in charge so far.

United have been in impressive form under the former United midfielder and head into facing Bournemouth on Friday night in third place in the Premier League.

Analysis by Manchester United correspondent Mark Critchley

International careers revived in the morning, club futures close to being settled come the afternoon. The turnaround in Harry Maguire and Kobbie Mainoo’s fortunes has been remarkable — not just over the course of the day, but over the past few months.

The prospects of Maguire extending his Old Trafford career beyond the end of this season were in the balance in the autumn, when the odd start here and there under Ruben Amorim was disrupted by injury.

Even when fit, the 33-year-old was distinctly behind Matthijs de Ligt in the running to start in the middle of Amorim’s back three.

In some ways, Mainoo’s future looked even bleaker. The United academy graduate did not start a single Premier League game under Amorim this season. Having pushed to leave during the final days of the summer window due to his lack of opportunities, a January exit appeared possible.

Yet since Michael Carrick took charge at the turn of the year, both have become ever-presents and have played integral roles in a run of seven wins in nine games that has made Champions League qualification not just a possibility, but a probability.

Maguire and Mainoo are two players at different points in their careers: one has had a prominent role in the club’s recent past, the other is a symbol of its future. But both have become key parts of United’s present again under Carrick, as the progress in these contract talks demonstrates.
